problem_text:
A logistics coordinator must allocate a set of critical electronic components to identical shipping crates for an international dispatch. The components are as follows:

* Component Alpha: mass 58 units
* Component Beta: mass 61 units
* Component Gamma: mass 44 units
* Component Delta: mass 47 units
* Component Epsilon: mass 68 units
* Component Zeta: mass 65 units
* Component Eta: mass 57 units
* Component Theta: mass 59 units
* Component Iota: mass 49 units
* Component Kappa: mass 58 units
* Component Lambda: mass 44 units
* Component Mu: mass 68 units
* Component Nu: mass 64 units
* Component Xi: mass 56 units
* Component Omicron: mass 36 units
* Component Pi: mass 56 units
* Component Rho: mass 55 units
* Component Sigma: mass 42 units
* Component Tau: mass 37 units
* Component Upsilon: mass 53 units
* Component Phi: mass 70 units
* Component Chi: mass 66 units
* Component Psi: mass 45 units
* Component Omega: mass 31 units
* Component Aleph: mass 62 units
* Component Beth: mass 34 units
* Component Gimel: mass 31 units
* Component Daleth: mass 56 units
* Component He: mass 52 units
* Component Vav: mass 42 units
* Component Zayin: mass 43 units
* Component Het: mass 51 units
* Component Tet: mass 57 units
* Component Yod: mass 36 units
* Component Kaf: mass 32 units
* Component Lamed: mass 61 units
* Component Mem: mass 57 units
* Component Nun: mass 49 units
* Component Samekh: mass 47 units
* Component Ayin: mass 54 units

Each reinforced crate has a strict maximum load capacity of 100 mass units. The objective is to assign every component to exactly one crate such that the cumulative mass within any given crate does not surpass its limit, while minimizing the total number of crates employed for the entire shipment.
